I have enough data to write up the report.

---

## Abstract

GEO series GSE309890 studies *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 (taxid 511145) exposed to sertraline in an adaptive-evolution experiment. GEO metadata registers 6 samples, an experiment type of "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing," and a single supplementary file that holds only processed FPKMs. The linked BioProject PRJNA1363958 (secondary study SRP644513) exposes 6 raw runs (SRR36018640–SRR36018645) on ENA, all paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000, library strategy `RNA-Seq`, library source `TRANSCRIPTOMIC`, library selection `cDNA`, totalling 69.1 M read pairs and 20.7 Gb of bases. The raw reads are therefore retrievable via ENA HTTPS FASTQ URLs. On the assembly question: the BRC Analytics Intergalactic Workflow Commission (IWC) catalogue lists 1 workflow under the ASSEMBLY category, `polish-with-long-reads-main`, which is a Racon long-read polishing step that requires an existing assembly plus Sanger/long reads and is not a de novo assembler. Additionally, these reads are cDNA (transcriptomic), not genomic DNA, so running a genome assembler on them would produce a transcript assembly rather than a genome. A reference genome for the exact strain is available at BRC (GCF_000005845.2), which is the more appropriate target for RNA-seq alignment or reference-based reassembly.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 profiles gene expression in *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 during adaptive evolution to the SSRI sertraline, comparing three control replicates against three 40-day evolved replicates. RNA-seq is the assay.

**Literature Review.** GEO reports no PubMed record linked to this series (`pubmed_ids: []`). No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** Whether the raw FASTQ reads for GSE309890 are publicly downloadable, and whether the BRC/IWC workflow catalogue offers an assembly workflow compatible with them.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: verify raw-read availability for GSE309890 and assess assembly-workflow fit. Expectation: because the GEO record labels the assay "high throughput sequencing" with a linked BioProject, raw reads should be mirrored on SRA/ENA; assembly appropriateness depends on library strategy and available workflows.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** GEO was queried for series metadata, then the linked BioProject was resolved to ENA to enumerate raw runs. The BRC Analytics organism/assembly catalogue and IWC workflow catalogue were queried to check for a compatible assembly workflow.

**Materials.**
- NCBI GEO (`geo_series`)
- ENA read-run portal via BRC federation (`brc_ena_study`)
- BRC Analytics organism/assembly catalogue (`search_organisms`, `get_assemblies`)
- IWC workflow catalogue (`list_workflow_categories`, `get_workflows_in_category`)

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890")` → series metadata, samples, BioProject link, supplementary files.
2. `brc_ena_study(study_accession="PRJNA1363958")` → run-level metadata and FASTQ HTTPS URLs.
3. `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655")` → no strain-level record; retried `search_organisms(query="Escherichia coli", limit=5)` → species record taxid 562.
4. `get_assemblies(taxonomy_id="562")` → reference assemblies.
5. `list_workflow_categories()` → assembly category count.
6. `get_workflows_in_category(category="ASSEMBLY")` → the single assembly workflow.

**Statistical Analysis.** Counts are direct field values from tool responses (`run_count`, `read_count`, `base_count`, `workflowCount`). No deduplication or derivation.

## III. Results

**Table 1. Raw sequencing runs for GSE309890 (ENA via BioProject PRJNA1363958 / SRP644513).**

| Run | Sample | Sample title | Layout | Platform | Read pairs | Bases |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SRR36018645 | SAMN53241894 | control, rep1 | PAIRED | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 11,621,726 | 3,486,517,800 |
| SRR36018644 | SAMN53241893 | control, rep2 | PAIRED | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 10,415,434 | 3,124,630,200 |
| SRR36018643 | SAMN53241892 | control, rep3 | PAIRED | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 11,720,219 | 3,516,065,700 |
| SRR36018642 | SAMN53241891 | adaptive evolution 40d, rep1 | PAIRED | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 11,992,461 | 3,597,738,300 |
| SRR36018641 | SAMN53241890 | adaptive evolution 40d, rep2 | PAIRED | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 11,997,182 | 3,599,154,600 |
| SRR36018640 | SAMN53241889 | adaptive evolution 40d, rep3 | PAIRED | Illumina HiSeq 4000 | 11,363,329 | 3,408,998,700 |
| **Total** | | | | | **69,110,351** | **20,733,105,300** |

All six runs report `library_strategy: RNA-Seq`, `library_source: TRANSCRIPTOMIC`, `library_selection: cDNA`.

**Table 2. FASTQ download URLs (paired-end, gzipped).**

| Run | R1 | R2 |
|---|---|---|
| SRR36018640 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018641 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018642 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018643 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018644 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018645 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_2.fastq.gz |

**Table 3. Assembly-related workflows in the IWC catalogue.**

| Category | Workflow count | Workflow ID | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASSEMBLY | 1 | polish-with-long-reads-main | Racon polish of an existing assembly with long reads (×4) |

**Findings.**
- Raw reads for GSE309890 exist and are downloadable: 6 paired-end Illumina runs on ENA totalling 69.11 M read pairs / 20.73 Gb.
- The library strategy for every run is RNA-Seq (cDNA), not genomic DNA.
- The IWC ASSEMBLY category contains 1 workflow, and it is a long-read polisher, not a de novo assembler; its required inputs are an existing assembly FASTA URL and long reads.
- A reference genome for the exact study strain is available: GCF_000005845.2 (K-12 substr. MG1655, complete, 4,641,652 bp, 1 chromosome, haploid).

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** Raw reads are available. However, running a genome assembly on them is not directly supported by the current IWC catalogue and is not the right analysis for the data type: the reads are cDNA short reads from *E. coli* transcriptomes, so a genome assembler would recover only expressed regions, and the sole listed ASSEMBLY workflow requires long reads plus an already-existing draft assembly.

**Context.** For this dataset the appropriate downstream routes in the BRC/IWC ecosystem are the TRANSCRIPTOMICS workflows (4 workflows listed) using the reference assembly GCF_000005845.2, or the VARIANT_CALLING workflows if the goal is to detect the *rpoBC*, *gyrAB*, and *tktA*-region mutations described in the series summary.

**Limitations.**
- GEO reports no linked PubMed record for GSE309890, so the study is unpublished or not yet indexed.
- BRC's organism search did not match the strain name directly; the species-level record (taxid 562) was used to enumerate assemblies.
- ENA `first_public` for the runs is 2026-02-22 in the returned metadata; access may still be embargoed for some clients even though the records resolve.
- The IWC catalogue is one workflow registry; other Galaxy or command-line assemblers (e.g. SPAdes, Trinity for transcripts) exist outside this catalogue and are not covered by these tool results.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** Yes to the raw reads, no to a de novo assembly through the currently listed IWC ASSEMBLY workflow. A sensible next query is `get_compatible_workflows(ploidies=["haploid"], taxonomy_id="511145")` and `get_workflows_in_category(category="TRANSCRIPTOMICS")` to select an RNA-seq quantification or variant-calling pipeline against GCF_000005845.2. If a genome assembly is truly desired, additional genomic-DNA sequencing (e.g. Illumina WGS or long reads) for the evolved strains would be needed and would then feed the long-read polishing workflow.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, series GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO FTP directory for GSE309890. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[3] ENA Portal API, filereport for PRJNA1363958. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport
[4] BRC Analytics organism/assembly catalogue (search_organisms, get_assemblies for taxid 562).
[5] BRC Analytics / IWC workflow catalogue (list_workflow_categories, get_workflows_in_category="ASSEMBLY"), workflow TRS ID `#workflow/github.com/iwc-workflows/polish-with-long-reads/main/versions/v0.1`.

## Acknowledgments

NCBI GEO and SRA (submitters of GSE309890 / PRJNA1363958); European Nucleotide Archive (EBI) for the FASTQ mirror; BRC Analytics for the organism, assembly, and workflow catalogues; and the Intergalactic Workflow Commission for the assembly workflow entry.
